key_insight: A forcing-informed resolvent analysis uses data-derived forcing and response subspaces to recover physically consistent input-output modes and gains in self-sustained unsteady flows.
engineering_relevance: It provides a data-driven way to identify where nonlinear forcing drives or damps flow fluctuations, improving reduced-order modeling and flow-control insight for complex CFD systems.
method: Estimate forcing and response bases from simulation snapshots.
Build a forcing-informed resolvent operator using these subspaces.
Extract paired forcing/response modes, gains, and a nonlinear energy transfer map.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on the Stuart-Landau oscillator and demonstrated on a 2D cylinder wake and a 3D transitional boundary layer, recovering mode pairs and gains even where nonlinear amplification is important.
watch_item: The method depends on representative snapshot data and accurate subspace estimation, so insufficient sampling or noise may weaken the extracted modes and energy-transfer interpretation.
paper_title: Forcing-informed resolvent analysis: Identification of input-output relations in self-sustained flows
